title: Well Done!
subtitle: Four ways to say congratulations
review: Text by the author; notes and questions written by Claude: check them. No Burmese yet.
intro: A light bulb changed after three months, a driver's license passed on the fifth try, a pancake that does not come back down and a new job to celebrate: four short scenes between Emma and Lucas. Listen for how they congratulate each other, and for the moments when they do not really mean it.

lines.text: I did it! I changed the light bulb!
lines.note: I did it! = I finished it, I was successful.

lines.text: Well done!
lines.note: Well done! praises something a person did.

lines.text: All by myself. No instructions.
lines.note: All by myself = with no help. Instructions: paper that tells you how to do it.

lines.text: Nice work! I'm impressed!
lines.note: Nice work! = well done. I'm impressed = I think it is very good.

lines.text: Are you making fun of me?
lines.note: Make fun of: laugh at someone.

lines.text: Not at all. Congratulations!
lines.note: Not at all = no, really.

lines.text: Thanks. It wasn't easy.
I know. I've been waiting three months.
lines.note: I've been waiting three months: she started three months ago and is still waiting.

lines.text: Lucas! I got my driver's license!
lines.note: Driver's license (American) = driving licence (British).

lines.text: No way! Congratulations! You earned it.
lines.note: No way! shows surprise. You earned it = you worked for it.

lines.text: On my fifth try…
lines.note: On my fifth try: she failed four times.

lines.text: Exactly. All that hard work paid off.
lines.note: Paid off = gave a good result.

lines.text: That's true.
I knew you could do it. You should be proud of yourself.
lines.note: I knew you could do it. Be proud of yourself: feel good about what you did.

lines.text: Thanks. Can I borrow your car?
lines.note: Borrow: take and give back later.

lines.text: … Congratulations. But no.
Watch! I'm gonna flip the pancake.
lines.note: Gonna = going to. Flip: turn over in the air.

lines.text: Go for it!
lines.note: Go for it! = try it!

lines.text: And… there!
Wow! You nailed it!
lines.note: You nailed it! = you did it perfectly. Informal.

lines.text: Wait, here's the second one. There!
Amazing! You've got this!
lines.note: You've got this! = you can do it.

lines.text: And the third one… Up it goes! … Where'd it go?
lines.note: Where'd it go? = Where did it go?

lines.text: It's on the ceiling. Way to go.
lines.note: Way to go = well done. Here Emma does not mean it: the pancake is on the ceiling.

lines.text: Big news! I got the job!
lines.note: Big news = important news. I got the job = they chose me.

lines.text: No way! That's great news!
lines.note: That's great news! News is singular: that is, not those are.

lines.text: I start Monday.
Congrats on the new job! I'm so happy for you!
lines.note: Congrats = congratulations. Informal. Congrats on + noun.

lines.text: Thanks, honey.
I'm proud of you. We should celebrate! Dinner out?
lines.note: I'm proud of you. Celebrate: do something special. Dinner out = dinner in a restaurant.

lines.text: Great idea! Your treat?
lines.note: Your treat? = are you paying?

lines.text: Oh, no. You're the one with the new paycheck.
lines.note: Paycheck (American): the money you get for your work.

notes: Well done!, Nice work! and Congratulations! praise a success. Congrats is short and informal.
Congratulations on + noun: Congrats on the new job. Congratulations on your wedding.
You earned it and All that hard work paid off praise the work, not only the result.
You nailed it!, You've got this! and Way to go! are informal. Use them with friends.
I'm proud of you and I'm so happy for you show your feelings.
Tone can change the meaning: Way to go, said flatly after a mistake, is not praise.

questions.q: Your friend passed an exam after months of study. You want to praise the work. What do you say?
questions.why: You earned it = you worked for this success.

questions.q: “All that hard work paid off.” What does paid off mean?
options: It cost a lot of money.
questions.why: Paid off = brought success in the end.

questions.q: The pancake is on the ceiling. Emma says “Way to go.” What does she mean?
options: She is joking: it went wrong.
questions.why: Way to go usually means well done. After a mistake, it is a joke.

questions.q: Emma asks “Your treat?” What is she asking?
